NATO in 2025

The [North Atlantic Treaty Organization](/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization "North Atlantic Treaty Organization") (NATO) is an international [military alliance](/wiki/Military_alliance "Military alliance") consisting of 32 [member states](/wiki/Member_states "Member states") from [Europe](/wiki/Europe "Europe") and [North America](/wiki/North_America "North America"). It was established at the signing of the [North Atlantic Treaty](/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty "North Atlantic Treaty") on 4 April 1949. Of the 32 member countries, 30 are in Europe and 2 are in North America. Between 1994 and 1997, wider forums for regional cooperation between NATO and its neighbours were set up, including the [Partnership for Peace](/wiki/Partnership_for_Peace "Partnership for Peace"), the [Mediterranean Dialogue](/wiki/Mediterranean_Dialogue "Mediterranean Dialogue") initiative, and the [Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council](/wiki/Euro-Atlantic_Partnership_Council "Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council"). The majority of NATO members are also [member states of the European Union](/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union").

All members have militaries, except for [Iceland](/wiki/Iceland "Iceland"), which does not have a [typical army](/wiki/Military_of_Iceland "Military of Iceland") (but it does have a [coast guard](/wiki/Icelandic_Coast_Guard "Icelandic Coast Guard") and a small unit of civilian specialists for NATO operations). Main article: [2014 League of Legends World Championship](/wiki/2014_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2014 League of Legends World Championship")

The 2014 World Championship featured 16 teams competing for a $2.13 million prize pool, with 14 teams qualifying from the primary *League of Legends* regions (China, Europe, North America, Korea and Taiwan/SEA) and two international wildcard teams. Riot stopped numbering seasons and instead simply used the year for the 2014 and future championships.

The group stage began on 18 September in [Taipei](/wiki/Taipei "Taipei") and concluded on 28 September in [Singapore](/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") with eight teams advancing to the bracket stage.[[23]](#cite_note-24) The bracket stage started on 3 October in [Busan](/wiki/Busan "Busan"), South Korea, and concluded on 19 October with the grand final hosted at the 45,000-seats [Seoul World Cup Stadium](/wiki/Seoul_World_Cup_Stadium "Seoul World Cup Stadium"),[[24]](#cite_note-25)[[25]](#cite_note-26) where South Korean team [Samsung Galaxy White](/wiki/Samsung_Galaxy_(esports) "Samsung Galaxy (esports)") beat the Chinese team Star Horn Royal Club to become the 2014 *League of Legends* world champions.[[26]](#cite_note-s4_results3-27) Support player Cho "Mata" Se-hyeong was named the tournament [most valuable player](/wiki/Most_valuable_player "Most valuable player") (MVP).

American band [Imagine Dragons](/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons") contributed the theme song "[Warriors](/wiki/Warriors_(Imagine_Dragons_song) "Warriors (Imagine Dragons song)")" for the tournament,[[27]](#cite_note-28) and performed live on the grand final stage in South Korea.[[28]](#cite_note-29) All games were made available for free via live streaming.[[29]](#cite_note-30)

The 2014 World Championship games were streamed live by 40 broadcast partners and cast in 19 languages. The grand final was watched by 27 million peopl

Further information: [Lincoln family](/wiki/Lincoln_family "Lincoln family")

Born in [a one-room log cabin](/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln_Birthplace_National_Historical_Park "Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park") in Kentucky on February 12, 1809, Abraham Lincoln was raised on [Sinking Spring Farm](/wiki/Sinking_Spring_Farm "Sinking Spring Farm") near [Hodgenville, Kentucky](/wiki/Hodgenville,_Kentucky "Hodgenville, Kentucky").[[3]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDonald199620–22-5)[[1]](#cite_note-anb-1) The second child of [Thomas Lincoln](/wiki/Thomas_Lincoln "Thomas Lincoln") and [Nancy Hanks Lincoln](/wiki/Nancy_Hanks_Lincoln "Nancy Hanks Lincoln"), he was a descendant of [Samuel Lincoln](/wiki/Samuel_Lincoln "Samuel Lincoln"), an Englishman who emigrated to [Massachusetts](/wiki/Massachusetts_Bay_Colony "Massachusetts Bay Colony") in 1637[[4]](#cite_note-6) (Abraham Lincoln said that Samuel Lincoln "came from Norwich, England, in 1638"[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurlingame2008vol._1_p._1-7)) and of the [Harrison family of Virginia](/wiki/Harrison_family_of_Virginia "Harrison family of Virginia").[[c]](#cite_note-9) His paternal grandfather and namesake, [Captain Abraham Lincoln](/wiki/Captain_Abraham_Lincoln "Captain Abraham Lincoln"), moved the family from [Virginia](/wiki/Colony_of_Virginia "Colony of Virginia") to Kentucky. The captain was killed in [a Native American raid](/wiki/Northwest_Indian_War "Northwest Indian War") in 1786.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurlingame2008vol._1_pp._1–4-10) The family settled in [Hardin County, Kentucky](/wiki/Hardin_County,_Kentucky "Hardin County, Kentucky"), in the early 1800s.[[8]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDonald199621–22-11) Nancy is widely assumed to have been the daughter of Lucy Hanks.[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBartelt20

The film wrapped up its run in American theaters on October 20, 2005,[[2]](#cite_note-Mojo-2) finishing with a total gross of $380,270,577. It ranks 29th in all-time domestic grosses and is the highest-grossing U.S. of 2005, out-grossing second-place *[The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe](/wiki/The_Chronicles_of_Narnia:_The_Lion,_the_Witch_and_the_Wardrobe "The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe")* by nearly $90 million.[[2]](#cite_note-Mojo-2) The film sold an estimated 59,324,600 tickets in the US.[[160]](#cite_note-170)

International grosses that exceeded $460 million include those Australia ($27.2 million), France and Algeria ($56.9 million), Germany ($47.3 million), Italy ($11.3 million), Japan ($82.7 million), Mexico ($15.3 million), South Korea ($10.3 million), Spain ($23.8 million), and the United Kingdom and Ireland ($72.8 million).[[161]](#cite_note-171) The total worldwide opening of *Revenge of the Sith* for each country was $254 million, combined with $304 million from its four-day weekend. It would go on to hold this record for two years before *[Spider-Man 3](/wiki/Spider-Man_3 "Spider-Man 3")* took it in 2007.[[162]](#cite_note-172)

Main article: [*How I Met Your Mother* season 9](/wiki/How_I_Met_Your_Mother_season_9 "How I Met Your Mother season 9")

With the exceptions of the series' 200th episode and the last episode, the entirety of season nine takes place in the 56 hours leading up to Barney and Robin's wedding.

Marshall, who is stuck in Minnesota, desperately tries to find a way to get to the wedding in time. Meanwhile, in Farhampton, the time is slowly counting down to the wedding, with a new problem arising in almost every episode. It is revealed that Lily is pregnant and that she and Marshall will have a daughter. It is also revealed that Ted's children are named Penny and Luke. In the 200th episode, the Mother's eight years before meeting Ted are revealed, while later episodes give viewers a glimpse of Ted and the Mother together in flash forward scenes. Also, Marshall uses his final two slaps from the slap bet: the first being used as an apology present for missing the rehearsal dinner, and the second when Barney begins to panic just before the beginning of the wedding ceremony.

In the series finale, it is revealed that after three years of marriage, Barney and Robin decided to divorce. Barney ends up later fathering a child during a one-night stand. Marshall eventually becomes a judge, and he and Lily have three children. Ted's wife, whose name is revealed to be Tracy McConnell, dies of an unknown illness in 2024, six years prior to the time of Ted telling his children the full story of how they met. Upon finishing the story, at the urging of his kids, Ted decides to ask Robin out. Alluding to the [first episode](/wiki/Pilot_(How_I_Met_Your_Mother) "Pilot (How I Met Your Mother)"), the finale ends with Robin, as she looks out of her apartment window to see Ted holding the blue French horn, smiling with tears in her eyes.

"Hollaback Girl" entered the [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") at number 82 on the issue dated April 2, 2005,[[34]](#cite_note-34) and within six weeks of its release, it had reached the top of the chart,[[35]](#cite_note-35) becoming Stefani's first and only US number one.[[36]](#cite_note-Hot100-36) It ended the nine-week run of [50 Cent](/wiki/50_Cent "50 Cent")'s "[Candy Shop](/wiki/Candy_Shop "Candy Shop")" featuring [Olivia](/wiki/Olivia_(singer) "Olivia (singer)"), and maintained the number-one position for four consecutive weeks.[[37]](#cite_note-37) "Hollaback Girl" ranked second on the [2005 Hot 100 year-end chart](/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2005 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2005").[[38]](#cite_note-US-yearend-38) The song held the record for most US radio airplays in one week, with 9,582 plays, and maintained this record for over a year before [Shakira](/wiki/Shakira "Shakira") and [Wyclef Jean](/wiki/Wyclef_Jean "Wyclef Jean")'s "[Hips Don't Lie](/wiki/Hips_Don%27t_Lie "Hips Don't Lie")" overtook the position.[[39]](#cite_note-39) "Hollaback Girl" peaked at number one on the *[Billboard](/wiki/Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* [Pop 100](/wiki/Pop_100 "Pop 100") chart for eight weeks and at number 15 on the [Hot Dance Club Play](/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") chart.[[40]](#cite_note-usp100-40)[[41]](#cite_note-usd-41) The song was a [crossover](/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") success and reached number four on the [Rhythmic Top 40](/wiki/Rhythmic_(chart) "Rhythmic (chart)") and number eight on the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](/wiki/Hot_R%26B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart.[[42]](#cite_note-usr-42)[[43]](#cite_note-usrandb-43)

"Hollaback Girl" was noted for having a large number of digital downloads, becoming the first single to sell more digital downloads than CDs.[[44]](#cite_note-RSMillion-44) In O

Main article: [Astro (South Korean band)](/wiki/Astro_(South_Korean_band) "Astro (South Korean band)")

Rocky debuted as part of the six-member boy group Astro on February 23, 2016, as a dancer and rapper of the group.[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11) On August 24, 2016, Rocky appeared in an episode of Mnet's *[Hit the Stage](/wiki/Hit_the_Stage "Hit the Stage")* where he portrayed *[The Mask](/wiki/The_Mask_(comics) "The Mask (comics)")*.[[12]](#cite_note-12) Rocky received praise from the judges, noting his expressions and movements as a perfect portrayal of the character.[[13]](#cite_note-star.mbn.co.kr-13)

On November 5, 2018, after four rounds of battle in 1theK's *Dance War*, Rocky was revealed to be Purple23 and placed second in the dance battle competition.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-한국경제티브이-15) On November 30, 2018, Fantagio Music released the digital single "STAR" which is a collaboration between Rocky and singer-songwriter Chawoo.[[16]](#cite_note-16) "STAR" was later included in the *FM201.8-11Hz* which was released on December 13, 2018.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

During Astro's second Astroad to Seoul "Starlight" concert which was held on December 22–23, 2018, Rocky performed his first solo song "Have a Good Day".[[18]](#cite_note-18) It was included in the DVD of the concert which was released in June 2019.[[19]](#cite_note-19) In 2019, Rocky self-composed one of the tracks from Astro's sixth EP, *Blue Flame*, titled "When the Wind Blows".[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21)

At the [92nd Academy Awards](/wiki/92nd_Academy_Awards "92nd Academy Awards"), *Avengers: Endgame* received a nomination for [Best Visual Effects](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Visual_Effects "Academy Award for Best Visual Effects").[[205]](#cite_note-Oscars-211) The film's other nominations include an [Annie Award](/wiki/Annie_Award "Annie Award") (which it won),[[206]](#cite_note-AnnieAwards-212) a [British Academy Film Award](/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Award "British Academy Film Award"),[[207]](#cite_note-BAFTA-213) and three [Critics' Choice Movie Awards](/wiki/Critics%27_Choice_Movie_Awards "Critics' Choice Movie Awards") (winning two).[[208]](#cite_note-CriticsChoice-214) Its [Wikipedia](/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia") page was [the most-viewed article of 2019](/wiki/Wikipedia:2019_Top_50_Report "Wikipedia:2019 Top 50 Report"), with 44.2 million views.[[209]](#cite_note-TopWikipediaArticle2019-215) *Endgame* ranked 41st in a March 2020 *[Empire](/wiki/Empire_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")* magazine poll of the 100 greatest films of the 21st century.[[210]](#cite_note-EmpireRanking-216) The [Avengers' assembling moment](/wiki/Avengers_assemble_scene "Avengers assemble scene") was one of five finalists for an Oscars Cheer Moment in the "[Oscars Fan Favorite](/wiki/Oscars_Fan_Favorite "Oscars Fan Favorite")" contest for the [94th Academy Awards](/wiki/94th_Academy_Awards "94th Academy Awards") in February 2022, despite the film's ineligibility for other Academy Awards that year.[[211]](#cite_note-OscarsCheerMoment-217)

Lead singer David Bayley stated that "Heat Waves" "is about loss and longing, and ultimately realising you are unable to save something".[[8]](#cite_note-8) He said that "Also, this song is about memories and it's very nostalgic, and sometimes people feel more of that in the winter. Maybe that's part of the reason this song's hung around for so bloody long – everyone's [locked inside](/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns") and trapped in their own thoughts."[[9]](#cite_note-USAT-9)

"Heat Waves" starts on a high and then drops into despair before rising again for a cheerful, optimistic finale, much like the crests and troughs of a real wave. Bayley came up with the chords one day while playing around on the guitar. He wrote the lyrics in just an hour, prompted by the death of a close friend whose birthday was in June.[[9]](#cite_note-USAT-9)

In March 2021, the podcast Song Exploder featured an interview with Dave Bayley that specifically discussed the creation of "Heat Waves". He says "weirdly, [Johnny Depp](/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp") was the first person to hear this song." In it, he says that after writing/performing the song late at night alone in the studio, he decided to go home when he realized a stranger was sitting behind him. It was Depp who had been working in another studio.[[10]](#cite_note-SongExploder-10)

Bayley also described the song’s production process in the same Song Exploder episode. He explained that the opening guitar riff originated as a phone recording before being developed into the track’s central motif. The arrangement was built by layering elements, including a pitched-down vocal sample used as the bass line. Bayley constructed the vocal harmonies from numerous takes, adding ad-libs to create what he called a “choir of myself.” He emphasized leaving space in the mix by stripping back certain sections so that the lead vocal and beat would stand out.[[10]](#cite_not
